lines: You do it every day, and scientists still are not sure *why*.
A yawn is a reflex: your jaw stretches wide, you take a long breath in, then a shorter one out.
It is ancient. Nearly all animals with a backbone yawn, and babies do it before they are born.
The old idea was that yawning brings in extra oxygen.
But in a nineteen eighty-seven study, people breathing air with extra carbon dioxide did not yawn more.
A newer idea: yawning may cool the brain, by pulling in cool air and speeding blood flow through the head.
In one test, people with a warm towel on their head yawned more than people with a cold one.
And across nineteen species, bigger brains came with longer yawns. Humans had the longest.
Then the strange part: [pause 100] seeing, hearing, or even reading about a yawn can set you off.
You are more likely to catch a yawn from family and friends than from strangers.
Chimpanzees catch yawns too. [pause 100] One idea is that it helps a group stay in sync.
